title: Musician, Horn (GySgt to Pvt) NMOS (5524), DIR COMM
raw_text:
16.     MOS 5544, Musician, Horn (GySgt to Pvt) NMOS (5524), DIR COMM

    a. Summary. Musicians perform in a Marine Corps Band for concerts,
parades, ceremonies, and various other official functions in support of the
Marine Corps Bands’ mission. Musicians perform additional duties in support
of band operations, such as unit supply, unit administrative assistant, and
music librarian. Musicians are required to perform preventative maintenance
on assigned musical equipment. Additional increased responsibilities
relating to music performance are assigned based on grade/experience, such as
instrument section leader or leader of a small ensemble. Musicians may be




                                          3-319                      Enclosure (1)
 3134                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



assigned to complete the Live Production Technician Course and be assigned
additional duties of sound engineer.

       b.   Prerequisites.    Must possess MOS 5524.

       c.   Requirements.    Must be proficient on the horn.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (be), Music Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Musicians and Singers 27-2042.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Member, "The President's Own," U.S. Marine Band, 5511.

            (2) Member, "The Commandant's Own," U.S. Marine Drum and Bugle Corps,
5512.
common_text: Marines in the Music OccFld provide music to support military ceremonies, official functions, community relations, personnel procurement programs, theater security cooperation, and troop "esprit de corps”. In combat, musical units continue musical functions and augment security on a temporary basis during periods of heightened combat intensity when use of the band in its primary role is impractical. Marines entering this OccFld will receive MOS 5500, Basic Musician. All OccFld 5500 MOSs are assigned and voided by authority of the CMC (MM). Marines enlisting under the Musician Enlistment Option Program (MEOP) U2 will be required to attend the Basic Music Course at the Naval School of Music (NSOM) after having completed recruit training and Marine Combat Training (MCT). Assignment to a Marine Corps Band follows successful completion of the Music Basic Course. Career Marine musicians will return to the NSOM for required advanced technical training or complete the Instrument Repair Course provided through a civilian school. The opportunity to participate in a formal apprenticeship program leading to receipt of department of labor certification of apprenticeship may be available in some MOSs within OccFld 55.

Marines in the Music OccFld provide music to support military ceremonies, official functions, community relations, personnel procurement programs, theater security cooperation, and troop "esprit de corps”. In combat, musical units continue musical functions and augment security on a temporary basis during periods of heightened combat intensity when use of the band in its primary role is impractical. Marines entering this OccFld will receive MOS 5500, Basic Musician. All OccFld 5500 MOSs are assigned and voided by authority of the CMC (MM). Marines enlisting under the Musician Enlistment Option Program (MEOP) U2 will be required to attend the Basic Music Course at the Naval School of Music (NSOM) after having completed recruit training and Marine Combat Training (MCT). Assignment to a Marine Corps Band follows successful completion of the Music Basic Course. Career Marine musicians will return to the NSOM for required advanced technical training or complete the Instrument Repair Course provided through a civilian school. The opportunity to participate in a formal apprenticeship program leading to receipt of department of labor certification of apprenticeship may be available in some MOSs within OccFld 55.

Musicians perform in a Marine Corps Band for concerts, parades, ceremonies, and various other official functions in support of the Marine Corps Bands’ mission. Musicians perform additional duties in support of band operations, such as unit supply, unit administrative assistant, and music librarian. Musicians are required to perform preventative maintenance on assigned musical equipment. Additional increased responsibilities relating to music performance are assigned based on grade/experience, such as instrument section leader or leader of a small ensemble. Musicians may be assigned to complete the Live Production Technician Course and be assigned additional duties of sound engineer. b. Prerequisites. Must possess MOS 5524. c. Requirements. Must be proficient on the horn. d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (be), Music Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
